results.name: free-drive

metrics.note_on_methodology: Two earlier attempts at this scenario are documented for transparency: (1) an initial waypoint-mode controller aimed at a far target saturated steer at +-1 continuously and just circled the car near spawn (never actually traveled, and grazed a pole, contributing to the separately-documented wasm OOB bonus finding); (2) this final version does a deliberate U-turn into the guaranteed-obstacle-free -Z half of the map, then a gentle (steerAmp 0.15, well within "mild input") figure-eight there for the rest of the 25s.

results.notes: U-turn into open ground (away from every obstacle, confirmed zero collision/panel damage), then a GENTLE (steerAmp=0.15) figure-eight-ish wander at throttle-driven speed for ~25s. FINDING: even this mild, sustained oscillating-steer input under continuous full throttle eventually (once the car reached high speed in top gear) flipped the car fully upside-down (minUpDot=-1.0) on perfectly flat, obstacle-free ground, after which speedKmh readings ballooned to unphysical values (up to 229.6km/h) consistent with a chaotic tumble/bounce rather than genuine road speed. This is a real vehicle-stability issue, independent of the separately-documented wasm crash bug.

results.name: BONUS: wasm-oob-crash-repro
results.notes: Reliable repro (2/2 runs) of a wasm RuntimeError "memory access out of bounds" in Body.getTransform() via stepVehicle(), triggered by sustained high-stress contact with a destructible object during hard alternating steering (hood panel broken, 3 panels loosened, 8020 dented vertices at the point of failure). Once triggered, EVERY subsequent stepN() call fails identically forever (confirmed via 2 consecutive post-crash pingStepAlive() calls) -- in the live game this presents as a silent total freeze (last frame stays on screen, console spammed every animation frame). See the final report for full detail.

results.name: ramp-jump
results.notes: honest finding: ramp is only ~8m from spawn + needs ~11m lateral travel to line up, so a fresh-launch approach at true 70km/h is geometrically tight (measured entry speed at 70km/h attempt: 71.7km/h). See per-attempt lateralMissM/allWheelsAirborneStepCount for whether each attempt actually landed on the ramp and got air.

results.name: reset-integrity
results.notes: each cycle: crash(90) + 2.5s, resetCar() (R), resetWorld() (Shift+R); PASS = damage state fully clears every cycle and liveHandleCount does not grow across the 15 cycles.

results.notes: stalled the page JS thread 3s (no rAF), then resumed; PASS = position/speed advanced only a small bounded amount (accumulator catch-up cap), not ~3s worth of driving, and no new console/page errors.

results.name: quality-cycling-under-load
